issues.issue: Did the RAD reasonably find the applicant not credible, given the lack of documents and his explanation for destroying them?
issues.applicant_position: No valid reason to doubt credibility; destroying documents was plausible; RAD cannot rely on lack of corroboration alone.
issues.respondent_position: Corroboration needed to offset negative credibility; no reasonable efforts to get documents; vague testimony properly weighed.
issues.result_quote: All in all there was ample reason for the RAD to come to the conclusions on credibility that it did.

issues.issue: Did the RAD misstate or selectively review the evidence on his Wabela relationship and the plausibility of leaving Ethiopia?
issues.applicant_position: RAD review was microscopic and selective; it misstated his testimony on Wabela and on his role in the case.
issues.respondent_position: RAD review was meticulous; points raised are minor, and the transcript shows no special friendship.
issues.result_quote: Even if it was overlooked it is not enough to overcome the balance of the testimony of the Applicant or counter the overall negative credibility findings.

issues.issue: Did the RAD ignore or unreasonably weigh the psychological report?
issues.applicant_position: RAD ignored the psychological report, which was raised in the appeal.
issues.respondent_position: Report was speculative advocacy, so RAD reasonably gave it little weight.
issues.result_quote: The psychological report was reviewed and found insufficient.
